recipes.name: Lemony Tahini Tagliatelle with Burst Cherry Tomatoes
instructions: Bring a large pot of generously salted water to a boil. Add the tagliatelle and cook to al dente according to the package instructions. Reserving at least 1 cup / 240ml of pasta water (more if you’d like flexibility), drain the tagliatelle and set aside.
In a large sauté pan, combine the crushed garlic, vegetable oil, panko, and salt. Toast over medium-high heat for about 5 minutes, stirring often, until golden. Transfer to a plate.
In the now-empty pan, heat the remaining vegetable oil over medium-high heat. Add the shallot and minced garlic and cook for about 5 minutes, or until soft and golden.
Add the tomatoes and cook for another 7 to 8 minutes, until lightly burst.
Meanwhile, in a medium bowl, whisk together the tahini, olive oil, lemon zest, lemon juice, nutritional yeast, maple syrup, and salt.
Slowly mix in the reserved pasta water to loosen the sauce*.
Add the tahini sauce to the pan with the tomatoes, then add the cooked pasta and peas. Toss to coat. Cook for 3 minutes to warm the peas through.
Stir in the basil just before serving.
Top with the toasted panko. Enjoy!

page_recipe_notes: Notes † Tahini can vary a lot between brands, especially in how much the sesame seeds are roasted. Some are made from raw sesame seeds and taste pretty mild, while others are made from toasted seeds, which gives them a far richer, deeper flavor. That’s the one you want here. The golden kind. * Start with 1 cup / 240ml and add more as needed, depending on how thick your tahini is.
Storage Store leftovers in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days. Note that the pasta sauce will dry as it cools. Reheat with a splash of water to loosen the sauce.
